# Send a daily Jira open-issues digest to Discord

**Pattern:** Schedule -> read -> filter -> summarise · **Level:** Production · **Trigger:** Schedule (daily)

## What it does
Reads Jira issues each morning, keeps the ones that aren't Done, and posts a grouped, counted digest to Discord — an async standup ready before anyone logs on.

## Why it exists
Live standups are expensive and board-checking is tedious. A daily digest gives the whole team the state of the board in one message, grouped by owner and tallied by status.

## Main flow
Every Morning 09:00 -> Get Jira Issues -> Keep Open Issues -> Build Digest by Assignee -> Format Message -> Post to Discord (failure -> error rail).

## Use it for
- A distributed dev team dropping the live standup
- A morning 'state of the board' post
- Daily stakeholder updates with no manual work

## You get
- A standup that writes itself
- Grouped by assignee, tallied by status
- One scheduled message vs everyone opening Jira

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Jira API token; Discord webhook URL.
Colour key: 🟦 entry · 🟫 app I/O · ⬜ logic · 🟩 output · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
This runs on a timer; the Jira read is pinned so you can preview the digest before connecting anything. Sample data is pinned on the trigger, so hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow end to end before attaching a single credential. Right-click → Unpin when you go live.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never bundled in a template. Every node that talks to an external service needs its own connection before the first real run — open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Jira API token**
Atlassian → account settings → Security → API tokens → Create. n8n's Jira SW Cloud credential takes your account email, the token, and your site URL (https://your-domain.atlassian.net).
_Gotcha:_ The token inherits your Jira permissions — it can only read/write projects your own account can access.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy Webhook URL. Paste it into n8n's Discord Webhook credential.
_Gotcha:_ A webhook URL is bound to one channel. Use a separate webhook/credential per channel you post to.

Set each credential up once; it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Nothing happens when the event should fire**
Cause: The workflow is still a draft, or its trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate it. The manual test URL is different from the production URL.

**A node shows a red triangle right after import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials note).

**The digest includes issues from every project**
Cause: issue:getAll returns everything the token can see.
Fix: Narrow it: add a JQL/project filter in the node options if your version supports it, or add a Filter on fields.project.key.

**'Done' issues still appear**
Cause: Your workflow's done status isn't literally named 'Done'.
Fix: Edit the Filter to your board's done status (e.g. 'Closed', 'Resolved').

**Provider returns 429**
Cause: You are hitting the API rate limit.
Fix: The node already retries with backoff; widen the schedule interval or lower the batch size to stay under quota.

Still stuck? The **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there.

## Design decisions

Open-ness is judged by a status Filter rather than trusting the API to pre-filter, because 'what counts as done' is board-specific and belongs in one obvious, editable place. Grouping by assignee (in one Code node) turns a flat issue list into an accountable standup. The per-assignee item list is capped at 8 so a busy board doesn't blow past Discord's 2000-char limit.

## Practice exercises

Already production-shaped — deepen it:

1. Add a JQL filter so the digest covers just the current sprint.
2. Post only issues that have been open more than N days (staleness report).
3. Split long digests into a thread of messages.
